input.answer:
I can't say which political party is to blame for high rents. Assigning blame is a judgment, and the StatCan tools only return statistics. They don't attribute housing outcomes to parties or governments.

My search for rent data turned up only commercial rent price indexes (tables 18-10-0255 and 18-10-0260), which cover office, retail and industrial buildings, not residential rents. The search was also flagged as weaker than usual, so I didn't pull residential rent figures. If you want, I can look for a residential rent table, such as average rent by city or the CPI rent component, and report the trends. Those numbers would show how rents have changed, but not who is responsible for the change.
